clue.text: Fellow with role behind bar

indicators.note: one thing behind another sits after it, so these letters follow in the answer

parts.note: a bar in a pub or shop is a counter
an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: A man whose job is to work behind the bar of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow' here is not a man but a matching equal, as in the fellow of a glove; 'behind' puts the role after the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterpart is the opposite number or equivalent of another, just as one glove is the fellow of its pair.

clue.text: Cinema of good renown oddly overlooked

indicators.note: if the odd-numbered letters are passed over, only the even-numbered ones remain

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A picture house with a fine reputation that nobody notices.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of GOOD RENOWN are O, D, E, O, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Odeon is a well-known British chain of picture houses, and the name came to stand for any grand movie theatre.

clue.text: Instinctive and obvious choice

definitions.meaning: first meaning: coming without being taught
second meaning: as a noun, the person or thing clearly suited

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is an adjective, the second a noun: someone who is 'a natural' is the obvious pick.
explanation.definitionFit: Innate talent is described with this adjective, and as a noun it names a candidate perfectly suited to some job.

clue.text: Lifted needle containing team's medicine

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting raises the letters so they read from bottom to top
to contain something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to needle someone is to irritate or rile them
a football or cricket team has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A syringe holding a sports squad's drugs is raised up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needle' looks like a noun, a syringe, but it is the verb meaning annoy. RI(XI)LE, read upwards, gives ELIXIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a medicinal potion, originally one supposed to cure all ills or prolong life.

clue.text: Soldier, man protecting leader of African country

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround and shield it, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: a guy is a man

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A soldier and another man guard the head of an African state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African country' reads as one phrase, but 'African' only supplies its first letter and 'country' alone is the definition, a South American one.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraguay is a landlocked nation in South America, lying between Argentina, Brazil and Bolivia.

clue.text: Painter, artist bound in retirement to purchase hotel

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the letters run backwards
to purchase is to take something in, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: a bound is a leap
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A retired artist, bound to buy a hotel, looks forward to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'obliged', but it is the noun meaning a jump. LEAP reversed is PAEL, which then takes in H.
explanation.definitionFit: Raphael was an Italian Renaissance master famous for his Madonnas and the School of Athens fresco.

clue.text: Redecoration of firm Ruth's been running

indicators.note: running suggests things in motion and disorder, so the letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written, the 's giving an S

explanation.surface: A company where Ruth is in charge has had its offices done up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' reads as Ruth managing the firm; it is the anagram signal for the thirteen letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A refurbishment is a renovation, restoring and smartening up a building or room.

clue.text: Pass boor, one cycling in New York

indicators.note: cycling goes round and round, so letters from the end come round to the front

parts.note: a gap is a mountain pass
a pleb is a coarse, common person
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rude person on a bike passes through a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' here is a gap between mountains, not a verb; with cycling, the last letters of the string wrap round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Apple is the long-standing nickname for New York City, popularised by jazz musicians and tourism campaigns.

clue.text: Intimate connections involving current well-known people

indicators.note: to involve is to include or take in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: intimate means personal, and connections are ties
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Close relationships linked to famous people of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day' qualifying the people; it is the physics symbol I, slotted between PERSONAL and TIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrities, especially from television or sport, are often called personalities.

clue.text: Stop discounting pair as competition

indicators.note: to discount something is to leave it out of the reckoning, so letters are dropped

parts.note: to stop something happening is to prevent it
PR is the abbreviation for pair

explanation.surface: Calling off a contest without counting a couple of entrants.
explanation.walkthrough: PR is a standard abbreviation for pair; take it from PREVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A single contest in a sports meeting, such as the high jump, is called an event.

clue.text: Jumps to it, regularly blocking wild river rushing in

indicators.note: something wild is unruly and out of order, so the letters are rearranged
a block sits in the middle of a passage, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: the letters of this word, rearranged and split around the inserted piece

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Someone leaps into action, stopping a fast-flowing river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumps to it' sounds like an order to hurry; it only supplies its even letters U, P, T, I, which sit inside IRR-VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Irruptive describes bursting or breaking violently into a place, which is forcible entry, the sense of irruption.

clue.text: Shocking Arsenal player misses header then French score, almost

indicators.note: missing the header means losing the top, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: Arsenal Football Club are nicknamed the Gunners

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: vingt is French for twenty, and a score is twenty

explanation.surface: An Arsenal footballer misses a header and France score: shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Header' and 'score' look like football; header is the first letter and score is the number twenty. Arsenal is a London football club whose fans and players are Gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unnerving takes away your courage and composure, just as a shock does.

clue.text: Gather, in Ancient Rome, you love sculptures primarily

parts.note: amas is Latin for 'you love', as in amo, amas, amat

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Gather round: back in Ancient Rome, you adored statues above all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Ancient Rome' tells you to put 'you love' into Latin, the second person of the verb every schoolchild chants.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or accumulate a large quantity of something over time.

clue.text: Insubstantial book Canadian singer pens

definitions.note: adjective for a noun; a bubble is something insubstantial

indicators.note: to pen is to shut in an enclosure, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: Michael Bublé is a Canadian crooner
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A Canadian singer writes a slight, lightweight book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pens' reads as writes; it means encloses. The accent on Bublé is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A bubble is a thin film of liquid around air, the very image of something flimsy and lacking substance.

clue.text: Walk in Westminster home of Polly perhaps

definitions.note: the first word of the street's name
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a London street running along St James's Park
second meaning: where a pet parrot lives

explanation.walkthrough: Birdcage Walk is a street in Westminster, London, beside St James's Park; Polly is the stock name for a parrot, and 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet parrot is traditionally called Polly and kept in a wire enclosure with a perch.

clue.text: State of panic, it's plain nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, the 's giving an S

explanation.surface: Someone in a panic is plainly crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' reads as a verdict on the panicking person, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailspin is literally an aircraft's spiralling dive, and figuratively a chaotic loss of control or emotional collapse.

clue.text: Brew mead and rare type of rum

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mixing honey wine with an unusual kind of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brew' reads as an instruction to make drinks; it shuffles the eight letters of the two words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara rum is a dark spirit distilled in Guyana along the Demerara river, which also names the brown sugar.

clue.text: Mischievous child wearing ribbon fished for crustaceans

indicators.note: something worn goes around its wearer, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: a ribbon is a strip or shred, as in 'torn to ribbons'
an imp is a naughty child

explanation.surface: A naughty child in a hair ribbon went fishing for shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ribbon' suggests something in the child's hair, but here it means a torn strip, as in 'cut to ribbons'.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrimp is to catch small prawn-like sea creatures with a net, so the past tense means went fishing for them.

clue.text: Capacity to save money raised, watch!

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising letters makes them read from bottom to top
to save something is to keep it safe inside, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: room is space or capacity
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A call to watch out for the ability to put cash aside.
explanation.walkthrough: RO(TIN)OM read upwards gives the answer; tin as slang for money is old British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To monitor is to keep observing something closely over time, which is what watching means here.

clue.text: Lucille, wrong about defending Big Brother creator

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters run backwards
a defender holds something within its lines, so the answer sits inside the words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words, ignoring the comma

explanation.surface: Lucille has got the author of the reality show all wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big Brother' suggests the reality TV show, but the creator is the novelist; read 'lucILLE WROng' backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell invented the all-seeing dictator figure Big Brother in his novel Nineteen Eighty-Four.

clue.text: Pick up dog holding neck, clipping coat

indicators.note: to hold something is to grip it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: Rover is the stock name for a dog

indicators.note: clipping an animal's coat strips off its outside, leaving only the middle letters

parts.note: the inner letters once the outer pair goes

explanation.surface: Lifting a dog by its scruff while giving it a trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipping coat' sounds like grooming the dog; it removes the outer letters of NECK.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up after an illness or slump is to get better, which is to regain health or strength.

clue.text: On horseback, through southern parts of Oxford?

parts.note: a rider who is up is mounted
per means by way of or through
S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: Riding through the southern districts of the university city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' suggests the city, but an Oxford is also a laced leather shoe; the question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: The top section of a shoe, above the sole, is called its upper, and an Oxford is a style of shoe.

clue.text: Wine President gets right away

indicators.note: sending something away removes it, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: Emmanuel Macron is President of France
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: The French President is served his wine straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets right away' reads as 'gets it immediately'; it means the R leaves MACRON.
explanation.definitionFit: Mâcon is a Burgundy wine from the area around the French town of that name, red or white.

clue.text: Trust social worker with child

parts.note: to trust that something will happen is to expect it
an ant is a social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: A council social worker looking after a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a council employee; it is an insect living in a colony. 'With child' is the definition, not a link word plus a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An expectant mother is one who is pregnant, the old phrase 'with child' meaning carrying a baby.

clue.text: Quarrel in school hard to ignore

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English private boarding school
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A row at school that is difficult to overlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarrel' wants to mean an argument, but it is also the bolt fired from a crossbow.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is a short square-headed bolt shot from a crossbow, a kind of projectile like the one a bow fires.

clue.text: Horrifying experience hearing two descriptions of Sadiq Khan?

indicators.note: something heard rather than read is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: he was knighted and is Mayor of London

explanation.surface: A frightening ordeal listening to people describe London's mayor.
explanation.walkthrough: Sadiq Khan, Mayor of London, became Sir Sadiq in 2022, so he is both a knight and a mayor; said together, those words make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare is a terrifying dream, and by extension any awful, distressing ordeal.

clue.text: Strip of grass church official cut

indicators.note: cutting something short trims off its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a verger looks after a church and leads processions

explanation.surface: A church official mowed a stretch of lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' reads as mowing the grass; it trims the last letter off VERGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A verge is the grassy border running alongside a road or path.

clue.text: Pope's line about corrupt revolutionary's threat to countryside

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: Urban is the name of eight popes, plus the 's

indicators.note: a revolution turns things right round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to warp is to pervert or corrupt
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A pope warns that a crooked radical is endangering rural life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a noun for a rebel; it turns WARP round, and L goes around the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban sprawl is the uncontrolled spread of towns into surrounding rural land, eating up farmland and green fields.
